thermal_time_constant.consequence: tau >> phase: the junction sees the TIME-AVERAGED flux; the in-phase peak is a PDN (IR) load, not a thermal one

hotspot.strip_verdict: PASS single-user: 0.921 W/mm2 time-averaged (A) vs 2.0 nominal and 1.0 conservative, no spreading credit. A sustained 100%-duty strip (prefill, saturated aggregate) in scenario A would be 3.924 W/mm2 > 2.0.

mitigation_if_sustained.choice: none needed for the single-user objective. For sustained duty: a strip duty governor (no area, no single-user latency) or a measured row-engine MAC energy below the threshold; the 0.9 GHz strip costs latency and still fails sustained, the deeper strip costs area the die does not have

hotspot.phy_verdict: r1 7.34 W/mm2 is IMPLAUSIBLE: it placed the whole 10.19 pJ/b HBM die share (controller, PHY both ends, ECC, on-die movement, control plane: SC'25 MI250X minus O'Connor) on the PHY footprint. Published host PHY energy 0.29-0.8 pJ/b gives 0.209-0.576 W/mm2 at the 0.9 TB/s peak and 0.126 W/mm2 averaged: PASS at every limit.
hotspot.controller_band_verdict: the 9.39 pJ/b residual of the unqualified 10.19 pJ/b HBM die share cannot be a controller-band charge: it would be 22.76 W/mm2 in phase, 5.8x the densest logic on the die. Bounded by logic density the band is <= 1.62 pJ/b and 0.862 W/mm2 time-averaged (PASS 2.0). In a GPU the residual is spent on the L2-to-controller fabric spread over the die; here it has no physical home. A measured controller energy replaces the bound.
hotspot.element_pnr_changes: none: 24 row-engines, 328.32 x 1,998 um frame, 1.2 GHz; size the element PDN for the in-phase current and report measured switching power
